items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: We did a Cy Coleman date because our bass player at the time, Bill Takas was Cy’s bass player and he contracted.

ctx.x: You found your way into the studio scene in New York?

Yeah. I always had that in the back of my mind that I wanted to do studio work. And Mulligan, well the Elgart band was a good entree into that, and Mulligan was a very good entree into that. I started doing — through another connection I started doing a lot of the rock & roll dates. And I got fairly busy doing those things. I was doing a Broadway show and I was playing Mulligan at Birdland and I was also doing dates during the day. And I started doing some jazz dates. We did a Cy Coleman date because our bass…

time, Bill Takas was Cy’s bass player and he contracted. So we did some Sauter- Finnegan things, we did Manny Albam, we did a number of the jazz writers. It was kind of a “get me the Mulligan band” these guys are good, let’s get as many of them as we can on this date and we know we have some good guys. I was — at that point I was juggling. And juggling is the name of — that’s the story of my life was juggling. Keeping Mulligan happy when I had to send a sub to the first set at Birdland every night because I was…
